title: The Night Watch
events_chronological: Terrified of being called up, Duncan and his friend Alec agree to kill themselves together, and Alec dies while Duncan is found alive.
Duncan is sentenced over Alec's death and sent to prison.
Viv begins an affair with a married soldier called Reggie, meeting him on crowded trains and in blacked-out streets.
Driving an ambulance through a night raid, Kay digs Helen out of the wreckage of a collapsed house.
Kay and Helen become lovers in the weeks after the rescue.
Kay and Helen keep a flat together, with Helen lying about small things and jealous of everyone Kay knew before her.
Helen meets Julia, who was Kay's lover years earlier, and the two begin an affair behind Kay's back.
Viv haemorrhages after an illegal abortion in a rented room, and Reggie leaves her there.
Kay finds Viv bleeding, gets her to a hospital, and slips her own gold ring onto Viv's finger so the nurses will treat her as a married woman.
Duncan shares a cell with Robert Fraser, a conscientious objector who argues with him about why he is really inside.
Kay lives alone in a lodging house, walking the streets in a man's clothes with nothing left to do.
Helen and Julia live together while Helen searches Julia's pockets and post for proof of an affair she cannot name.
Viv works at a marriage bureau and still meets Reggie in hotel rooms, keeping the borrowed gold ring in a drawer.
Duncan keeps house for an elderly man called Mr Mundy until Fraser turns up at the door and unsettles everything.
syuzhet_notes: The novel is in three dated parts running backwards: 1947 first, then 1944, then 1941. Told-order bullets 1-4 are the aftermath, 5-9 the war years that produced it, and 10-14 the beginning of everything.
fabula_notes: Chronology is unambiguous because each part is dated. Inside a part the narration moves forward, so the reversal is at the level of the parts rather than the sentences.
